steps: Rinse the poha in a strainer two or three times, drain, and leave it for 5 minutes to soften.
Sprinkle the salt, sugar and turmeric over it and mix lightly with your fingers.
Heat the oil and fry the peanuts until crunchy, then lift them out onto a plate.
In the same oil let the mustard seeds pop, then add the cumin, a pinch of hing and the curry leaves.
Fry the onion and green chilli until the onion turns soft and see-through.
Add the small potato cubes, cover, and cook on low heat until tender.
Add the poha and peanuts, toss gently, cover and steam on very low heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Squeeze lemon over it, scatter coriander leaves and serve hot.
note: Curry leaves and fried peanuts are now in, as every Maharashtrian kanda poha has them; peanuts are 10 g a plate, between the two sources. Potato is cut to 50 g so the onion stays the star, and the optional grated coconut is left out.
